#en: I am starting to think the worst damage on a SysDef ship never shows up on a hull scan. It is in the tiny gaps between what one person meant to say and what the next person actually heard. Naomi Khatri swore she logged the last change to our patrol lanes; Leah Ortiz insists she never saw it. Erin Cho thought Command's burst about "legacy triage assets" was just another dead file bouncing around the network. I thought the medic they flagged was a ghost story to keep us sharp on watch.\n\nToday, HM-7378 dropped out exactly where the amended orders said to, only to find a medical courier wreck that is not on any official chart and a string of reroutes buried under half a decade of "we will fix it later." Comms traffic does not quite line up with the nav logs, and nobody can explain why our previous shift burned three hours loitering off a rock that does not appear in the briefing. None of it is big enough on its own to raise an alarm, but all together it feels like we have been nudged, a few degrees at a time, into someone else's forgotten emergency response. If this is just a paperwork snarl, it is the most elaborate one I have ever seen.
zh: 我开始觉得，一艘星防队船上最严重的损伤从不出现在船体扫描上。它在一个人打算说的话和下一个人实际听到的话之间那些微小的缝隙里。娜奥米·卡特里赌咒说她记录了我们对巡逻航道做的最后一次改动；莉亚·奥尔蒂斯坚称她从没见过。艾琳·乔以为指挥部那条关于"遗留分诊资产"的急电只是又一份在网络上弹来弹去的死文件。我以为他们标记的那名军医只是一个让我们值勤时保持警醒的鬼故事。\n\n今天，HM-7378 恰好在修订后的命令所说的位置跃出，却只发现一艘不在任何官方星图上的医疗快船残骸，以及一连串埋在五年"我们回头再修"底下的改道记录。通讯流量与导航日志对不太上，也没人解释得清为什么我们上一个班次会在一颗简报里根本不存在的岩石外空转三个小时。单看每一件都不足以拉响警报，可合在一起，感觉我们正被一点一点、每次几度地推入别人早已遗忘的应急响应里。如果这只是一团文书上的乱麻，那它是我见过的最精心编织的一团。

#en: Some nights I think half the Settled Systems lives off lies told in cargo bars. Gagarin is proof. Every time I ask about those lost convoys I get a different version, sanded smooth by whoever is talking. Dock clerks swear the lanes were straight and certified. Haulers over Erdebrau insist the routes kinked at the last second into the same patch of bad sky. No one ever agrees on details, just on one thing; it was not their fault. You can feel it in the way the story edges keep getting rounded off, like they have all told it too many times to themselves already.\n\nI started copying manifest numbers on the sly, lining them up against what little GalBank will still show, and the more I look the less the official record matches what people mutter in backrooms. Insurance spikes on runs that were supposedly uneventful. Traffic traces that look like someone took a handful of convoys and nudged them, just a little, onto the same strange three-forked pattern. Nobody wants to say the name tied to those adjustments out loud, but when it does slip through their teeth, it comes out soft, like they are afraid he might be listening on an open channel.
zh: 有些夜里我觉得，定居星系群有一半是靠货运酒吧里说的谎活着的。加加林就是证明。每次我问起那些失踪的运输队，都会得到一个不同的版本，被说话的人打磨得光滑圆润。码头文员赌咒说那些航道笔直且经过认证。喝着埃尔德啤酒的运货船员坚称航线在最后一秒拐进了同一片坏天空。细节上从来没人一致，只在一件事上一致：那不是他们的错。你能感觉得到故事边缘是怎么一直被磨圆的，像他们早就对自己讲了太多遍。\n\n我开始偷偷抄下清单编号，拿它们和盖尔银行还肯显示的那点东西对照；我越看，官方记录就越和人们在密室里嘟囔的东西对不上。那些据说平平无奇的航次却保险费用飙升。交通轨迹看起来像有人抓起一把运输队，轻轻一推，就推到同一个奇怪的三叉图案上。没人愿意大声说出与那些调整有关的名字，可当它真从他们牙缝里溜出来时，总是很轻，像他们害怕他可能正在某个公开频道上听着。

#en:
I was not supposed to take the job. Should have left that low-grade Alliance posting to some green kid with a patched suit and big dreams. But a derelict signaling from nowhere smells like clean salvage, and clean salvage pays.  

The shuttle was wrong the second I saw it. Hull creased in directions metal does not like to bend, cockpit torn open from the inside, like the jump itself had tried to eat its way out. I buried what was left of the pilot with my gloves still on, dust clinging to the suit, then found his slate half-melted under a rock he had not finished stacking.  

There was enough data left to scrape together a name, the same one I heard once in a bar on Gagarin when freighter captains got too drunk to watch their tongues. Short, sharp, the way spacers talk about storms. Nav noise on his last jump matched an old ghost blip I logged years back and forgot, filed under sensor glitch to keep dispatch off my back.  

Funny how the past leaves fingerprints on the present. One bad reading ignored, one rumor laughed off, and suddenly the lines all converge on a single path someone has been penciling into the dark for a long time.
zh:
我本不该接这份活。本该把那个低级别的联盟岗留给某个穿着打补丁制服、满怀梦想的毛头小子。可一艘从虚无中发出信号的弃船闻起来就像干净的打捞，而干净的打捞能挣钱。

那艘穿梭机我一看到就觉得不对。船壳朝金属不喜欢弯的方向折皱，驾驶舱是从里面被撕开的，像跃迁本身试图从里往外吃出一条路。我戴着还没脱的手套把飞行员剩下的东西埋了，灰尘黏在制服上，然后在他还没堆完的一块石头底下找到了他那块半熔的数据板。

剩下的数据还够我拼凑出一个名字，正是我有一次在加加林的酒吧里听过的那个——那会儿货船船长们醉得管不住舌头。短促、锋利，就像太空人谈起风暴时那样。他最后一次跃迁的导航噪声，与我多年前记录过又忘掉的一个旧幽灵信号吻合；我当时把它归到传感器故障下，好让调度别再烦我。

有趣的是，过去如何在现在身上留下指纹。一个被忽略的坏读数、一则被一笑而过的传言，忽然之间，所有线索都汇聚到一条有人早已在黑暗中用铅笔描了很久的路上。

#en:
I keep telling myself it is coincidence.

One farmer comes in, says his arm rig locked during harvest. Glitch, fine. Next week a hauler swears her vision implant fuzzed out right as she hit orbit. Different clinic, different brand, same shrug from the rep on the other end of the line. I log it, because that is what I do out here in the tin box while the real decisions get made in cities I will never see.

Then the numbers start to rhyme.

Same fragment in the diagnostics, same vague reference to an "independent tech," same way people drop their eyes when I ask who did the install. They stop saying names, start pointing with their chins, like the old days when you did not say a gang's tag out loud. The complaints get marked resolved upstairs, but they keep walking through my door, shaking, scared, angry.

Tonight I laid the reports out on the desk and followed dates and coordinates with my finger until the trail curled back on itself. Too many accidents lining up on the same curve for me to call it bad luck anymore. Coincidences stacked until they leaned, and once they leaned they pointed, and now I cannot pretend I do not see where.
zh:
我一直告诉自己这是巧合。

有个农民来了，说他收获时手臂义肢卡死了。故障，好吧。下周一个运货船员赌咒说她的视觉植入体在她刚进入轨道时糊掉了。不同的诊所，不同的品牌，电话那头代表同样的耸肩。我记下来，因为我在这只铁盒子里干的就是这个，而真正的决定是在我永远不会见到的城市里做出的。

然后那些数字开始押韵。

诊断里同样的片段，同样含糊地提到"一名独立技师"，同样在我问是谁装的时人们垂下眼睛的样子。他们不再说名字，开始用下巴指方向，像从前你不敢大声报出某个帮派名号的日子。投诉在楼上被标成已解决，可它们仍不断从我门口走进来，发抖、害怕、愤怒。

今晚我把报告铺在桌上，用手指顺着日期和坐标追下去，直到那痕迹绕回到自己身上。太多事故落在同一条曲线上，我再也不能称之为运气不好了。巧合越堆越歪，而一旦歪了，它们就指向了某个方向；如今我不能再假装自己看不见它指向哪里。

#en:
I think this is still the Ananke Drift, but the nav keeps flickering like it does not want to admit we are really here. Suits me fine. No one likes logging this rock anyway.

Met the Aegis man today. He did not say Aegis, but you can hear it in the way he measures every word, like he is still on record even when his badge is gone. Face looked like he had not slept since the coolant incident everyone avoids naming directly. Ask three people what happened and you get three stories, all framed to make sure no one in uniform comes back with questions. Nobody pushes too hard; out here, curiosity is just a slower way to die.

He handed me a cracked slate, said he was "done chasing ghosts." The trace on it is not a ghost, though. It is a route signature, buried under maintenance pings and survey sweeps, repeating at intervals that match a very real ship. I crosschecked it with what little I have: that stray dataslate from the fringe homestead, the harvest that grew too well, and the way a certain name keeps surfacing in dockside rumors whenever someone mentions miracle grain and missing logs. Wherever that pattern leads next, it is not random.
zh:
我想这仍然是阿南刻漂流带，可导航一直闪个不停，像不愿承认我们真的在这里。随它去吧。反正没人喜欢记录这块岩石。

今天见到了那个神盾的人。他没说神盾，可你听得出来——他每个字都掂量过，像哪怕徽章没了，他仍在被记录着。他的脸看起来像自那次人人都避免直接点名的冷却液事故以来就没睡过。你问三个人发生了什么，会得到三个版本，每个都编排得确保没有一个穿制服的人会带着问题回来。没人逼得太紧；在这外面，好奇心只是死得慢一点的方式。

他递给我一块裂了的数据板，说他"不再追鬼了"。可上面的踪迹不是鬼。那是一个航路特征，埋在维护探测和勘测扫描底下，以与一艘真实存在的飞船相符的间隔重复着。我拿手头仅有的东西交叉核对：来自外缘农庄的那块游离数据板、那次长势过好的收成，以及每当有人提起奇迹谷物和失踪日志时某个名字如何在码头传言中一再浮出。不管那图案下一步通向哪里，它都不是随机的。

#en:
I keep replaying that day on the outpost like a bad grav sim with a glitching reset. It was supposed to be routine: check the soil monitors, log the yields, complain about funding over cold TerraBrew. I saw the anomaly in the routing table, a little flag on a grain shipment that did not match the standard template. I remember thinking, "must be some clerk in Gagarin fat-fingering codes again," and I let it sit until after lunch.

By then the recall order had appeared and vanished in the queue, just a flicker. The samples still went out.

I told myself it was nothing, that people above my pay grade knew what they were doing. Then reports started drifting back months later, in rumor not in data: colonists coughing up dust, fields that would not stop producing even after the farmers begged for a fallow cycle. Someone down the chain kept calling it a miracle. Someone up the chain kept insuring it. I keep wondering if I had overridden that single shipment, forced a manual review, whether any of this would still be happening, or if they would have just found another technician too tired to double-check a harmless little deviation in the code.
zh:
我在脑子里一遍遍重放前哨站的那一天，像一段重置故障的糟糕重力模拟。那本该是例行公事：检查土壤监测器、记录产量、就着冷掉的地球酿酒抱怨经费。我在航路表里看到了那处异常，一个谷物货件上的小标记，不符合标准模板。我记得自己当时想"肯定又是加加林哪个文员打错了代码"，然后就让它在一边搁到了午饭后。

到那时，那份召回命令在队列里出现又消失了，只闪了一下。样品还是发走了。

我告诉自己没什么，薪水比我高的人知道他们在做什么。可几个月后，报告开始慢慢飘回来——是在传言里，不是在数据里：殖民者咳出灰尘，田地在农民求着要休耕一季之后仍不肯停止产出。链条下端有人一直称之为奇迹。链条上端有人一直为它投保。我总在想，要是我当初否决了那一单货、强制执行一次人工复核，这一切是否还会发生，还是他们只会再找一个累得不会去复查代码里一点无害小偏差的技师。

#en:
I am done pretending this is random.

When I took this posting on the rock, it was supposed to be easy time. Push manifests, skim a little off the top, sign whatever the system fed me. Then the "variance" jobs started showing up. Same ship classes, same lanes, always shifted a hair off the standard corridor. Escorts dropped by just one hull. Refuel stops quietly deleted. First one, I thought the clerk before me was lazy. Fifth one, I told myself the computer was glitching. Twentieth, and my hands were shaking every time I hit confirm.

Tonight I dug deeper. Buried in the routing tables was an old UC code woven through the edits, a reference tag that should not exist on a backwater module like this. I followed it, line by line, until it pointed at a forgotten military node out-system, one of those posts they "decommissioned" on paper and left to rot in the dust. All my altered lanes bend toward it, like someone has been curving traffic around a blind spot for years and paying idiots like me to press the button.

I thought I was just helping cargo dodge fees and inspections. Turns out I have been nudging people onto a board I cannot even see.
zh:
我不再假装这是随机的了。

我接下这块岩石上的岗位时，那本该是段轻松日子。推推清单，从顶上揩点油，系统喂给我什么就签什么。可后来"偏差"类的活儿开始冒出来。同样的船级、同样的航道，总是偏离标准走廊一丝。护航船少了一具船体。补给停靠被悄悄删掉。第一单，我以为是我前任文员太懒。第五单，我告诉自己电脑出故障了。第二十单，我每次按下确认键时手都在抖。

今晚我挖得更深。埋在航路表里的，是一个织进那些改动中的旧联殖代码，一个不该存在于这么个穷乡模块上的引用标签。我一行行顺着它追下去，直到它指向系统外一座被遗忘的军事节点——那种他们纸面上"退役"、却任其在尘土里烂掉的据点。我所有被改动的航道都朝它弯过去，像有人多年来一直在把交通绕着一处盲区弯过去，还付钱给像我这样的白痴去按那个按钮。

我以为我只是在帮货物躲开费用和检查。结果我一直在把人推上一块我自己都看不见的棋盘。

#en:
I keep replaying that survey run in my head, the one that brought us down to this nobody rock. We were behind schedule, two drones already fried by static, so when the air samplers started flashing out-of-range, I just tagged the readings as localized contamination and pushed on. No budget for curiosity. We scraped a few cores, logged coordinates, lifted before the storm front ate the landing gear.  

Weeks later, back on the station, those same samples showed a pattern that did not match any refinery waste or colony runoff. A precise kind of wrong, like someone had been drawing lines through the atmosphere with a scalpel. I filed a note to Environmental, then watched it vanish under "non-critical." Ships kept jumping through the sector, captains grumbling about minor course corrections, nothing more.  

Now I have seen the half-burned log from that outpost, heard the nervy chatter about a freighter that never arrived, and skimmed the vault ship manifests that almost make sense if you ignore the gaps. It feels like whatever she did down there started as a rushed test, a small cheat in the math, and we all stepped over the stain without looking down.
zh:
我脑子里一直在重放那次勘测航行，就是那次把我们带到这块无人岩石上的。我们落后于进度，两架无人机已经被静电烧掉了，所以当空气采样器开始闪出超范围时，我只是把读数标成局部污染就继续了。没有预算供你好奇。我们刮了几个岩芯、记录了坐标，在风暴锋面吃掉起落架之前升空了。

几周后回到空间站，同样那些样本显示出一种不符合任何精炼厂废料或殖民地径流的图案。一种精确的"错"，像有人一直在用手术刀在大气里画线。我给环境部门提了个条子，然后眼看它在"非关键"底下消失。飞船继续跃过那个星区，船长们嘟囔着些微的航向修正，仅此而已。

如今我看过了那座前哨站半烧毁的日志，听过了关于一艘从未抵达的货船的紧张闲聊，也翻过了那些只要忽略空白就几乎说得通的金库船清单。感觉她在那下面做的一切，都是从一次仓促的测试、一次算式上的小小作弊开始的，而我们全都从那块污渍上跨了过去，没有低头看。

#en: I keep telling myself the array is just old hardware and lazy clerks, but sitting in this cramped console seat, listening to the static between pings, it feels more like I am eavesdropping on a lie everyone agreed not to talk about. The corridor it watches is not on any chart I can pull without favors, yet the sensors know it is there; tiny grav spikes, ships sliding through at angles that make my stomach tighten just looking at the vector math. Traffic control tagged them as calibration drift years ago and then, somehow, never circled back. Funny how nobody quite remembers who filed the original note, or why the budget never stretched far enough to decommission the array outright. I have seen that same silence before: at a frontier dock where a captain "lost" half his jump logs, in a station bar where people changed the subject as soon as Neon's power dips came up, in a maintenance bay where a tech swore she had never met a pilot named Vector but could trace his burns on the hulls she patched. Now this old watcher is staring straight down the throat of a path he is been rehearsing, and every omission around it feels less like ignorance and more like consent.
zh: 我一直告诉自己，那组阵列只是老旧硬件和懒惰文员的问题，可坐在这张逼仄的控制台座椅上，听着探测之间的静电，感觉更像是我在偷听一个大家都约定不谈的谎言。它所监视的那条走廊不在任何我不托人情就调得出的星图上，可传感器知道它在那里；微小的重力尖峰，飞船以一些单是看矢量算式就让我胃部收紧的角度滑过。交通管制多年前把它们标成校准漂移，然后不知怎的再没回头看过。有趣的是，没人太记得是谁提交了最初那份说明，也没人记得为什么预算始终不够把整组阵列彻底退役。我见过同样的沉默：在一座边疆船坞，一位船长"弄丢"了他一半的跃迁日志；在一间空间站酒吧，霓虹城电力骤降的话题一起，人们就换了话题；在一处维护舱，一名技工赌咒说她从没见过一个叫"向量"的飞行员，却能把她修补过的船壳上他的烧痕认出来。如今这名老守望者正死死盯着他一直在演练的那条路的咽喉，而它周围每一处沉默，都越来越不像无知，更像默许。
